title: Modal Auxiliary Verbs: Introduction (Quiz 208)
content:
## Modal Auxiliary Verbs: Introduction (Quiz 208)

An introduction to modal auxiliary verbs, including the paired forms can/could, may/might, shall/should, and will/would, plus five single forms.

### Understand the pattern

Core modals include can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would and must. They express meanings such as ability, permission, possibility, obligation and advice. They normally take a base verb and do not add -s for he or she.

### Worked answers and explanation

She can swim, not 'she cans swim' or 'she can to swim'. The archive card also lists ought to, need, dare and used to. These related expressions do not all behave like core modals: need and dare can act as ordinary verbs, ought includes to, and used to describes a past habit or state.

### Try another

Correct: He must to finish the exercise.

### Suggested answer

He must finish the exercise. After the core modal must, use the bare infinitive finish. A negative is formed directly, as in must not finish, without adding do.
